transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lila Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Skyline Head of Data), Ethan Ross (Skyline CTO), Maya Li (Skyline Security), Samir Khan (Skyline AI Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick Console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route cost breakdown, and compliance hooks. Customer wants POC for cost validation and compliance review.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lila Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out time. I'm Lila from Redwood, this is Marco and Jordan on the SE side. How are you all?
[00:08] Priya Patel: Good, thanks. Excited to see the console — we're specifically there to understand cost per route and how to surface anomalies.
[00:14] Ethan Ross: Yeah, and security too, so Maya will ask the heavier questions.
[00:18] Maya Li: Hi, thanks. I'll probably jump in when you hit audit logs and encryption.
[00:22] Marco Alvarez: Great, quick agenda: run through usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and then Q&A and next steps. We'll also show how alerts and RBAC look.
[00:30] Jordan Patel: I'll share my screen — can everyone see the console?
[00:33] Samir Khan: Seeing it now, small lag but ok.
[00:36] Marco Alvarez: Cool. First frame is the overall token consumption heatmap, time series, and cost. You can filter by model, route, and environment. So here you can see daily cost, token counts, and average latency per route.
[00:48] Priya Patel: Quick question — does the cost on this dashboard include dedicated GPU amortization or just per-request charges?
[00:54] Marco Alvarez: Good question. By default the hosted view shows per-token usage cost plus infra overhead; for Dedicated we show committed capacity amortized across routes and you can toggle to see reserved versus burst usage.
[01:05] Maya Li: And where is customer data retained? Audit logs — how long?
[01:09] Marco Alvarez: Audit logs are retained configurable up to 13 months for enterprise tenants; by default it's 90 days. We have S3 archival and export hooks to your own bucket for longer retention.
[01:19] Ethan Ross: Can we get a view per route, like "claims-processing" vs "triage-bot"?
[01:23] Jordan Patel: Yes — jumping into per-route dashboard now — here's route list, you can click into a route and see token distribution, top prompts, latency p95, cost per invocation.
[01:33] [01:33] Marco Alvarez: Notice the cost attribution table — tokens, compute time, KV cache hits. Cache hits reduce cost per token because we don't re-generate prefixes.
[01:41] Priya Patel: Hmm cache hits — is that across routes or per-route?
[01:44] Marco Alvarez: It's per-route but you can enable global prefix caching across compatible routes; we surface cross-route cache effectiveness in the analytics.
[01:52] Samir Khan: Important for us, we have a lot of similar prompts across teams.
[01:56] Marco Alvarez: Exactly — and Optimize can recommend batching and quantization profiles for heavy routes, we can show suggested savings.
[02:04] Lila Chen: On the right, you can see our cost breakdown widget — split by model variant, quantization, and infra tier. It shows an estimated per-1M-token cost and the contribution by route.
[02:14] Priya Patel: That per-1M number — how accurate is it? We need it to plan budgets.
[02:18] Marco Alvarez: It's an estimate based on your historical mix; for POC we run a short benchmark to produce a calibrated estimate with your input traffic. Usually within 5-10% of actual during the observed window.
[02:29] Ethan Ross: Ok, that's helpful. What about alerts? We want to detect cost regressions when a new prompt ramp causes token explosion.
[02:36] Jordan Patel: You can set alerts on token delta, cost spikes, latency regressions; there's an auto-detect model that finds outliers in prompt length distribution.
[02:44] Maya Li: Does that alert tie into our PagerDuty or Slack?
[02:47] Marco Alvarez: Yep, integrations with PagerDuty, Slack, and webhooks. Audit events are logged for alert triggers too.
[02:53] Priya Patel: On permissions: can we restrict who sees cost data? Some teams shouldn't see raw prompt text.
[02:57] Lila Chen: RBAC supports route-level view permissions and you can mask prompt text except for admin and audit roles. We also support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[03:07] Maya Li: Encryption — at rest and in transit? KMS?
[03:10] Marco Alvarez: TLS in transit, envelope encryption at rest. For Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM. We can provide key rotation policies and HSM-backed keys for on-prem.
[03:21] Ethan Ross: Good. For the POC we'd likely want Dedicated so we can reproduce latency and throughput. How do you recommend sizing?
[03:27] Marco Alvarez: If you share sample QPS and sequence lengths, we can map to our performance profiles. For example, 25 QPS with avg 1k tokens and p95 latency target of 300ms maps to X GPUs — Marco points at the table on the screen — and we can reserve burst capacity.
[03:40] Samir Khan: We'll add sample traffic to the sheet later.
[03:42] Priya Patel: Can you also show the per-route SLA reporting?
[03:45] Jordan Patel: Sure — here's the per-route SLA widget; you can see uptime, error rates, and a rolling window for latency SLOs. We also show the fallback behavior if a model variant is unhealthy — it will route to a compatible cheaper variant per your policy.
[03:58] Lila Chen: One example we've seen: customers set a cost ceiling and automatic fallback to a quantized variant when cost > threshold — keeps UX up while saving budget.
[04:08] Priya Patel: Does that impact quality? We need to track hallucination/regression.
[04:12] Marco Alvarez: Yes that's why we tie quality monitors: when you enable a fallback, we run lightweight evals on a sample prompt set and compare metrics; if quality drops below threshold it can auto-roll back.
[04:22] Maya Li: We need audit trails for any auto-rollbacks for compliance. Is that logged?
[04:25] Marco Alvarez: Logged with before/after model IDs, timestamp, and operator — all searchable in the audit log.
[04:31] Ethan Ross: On cost allocation across business units, can we tag routes to chargeback codes?
[04:36] Jordan Patel: Yes tags and label-based cost grouping. Exportable to your FinOps tooling.
[04:40] Priya Patel: How do you compute the infra amortization for Dedicated?
[04:43] Marco Alvarez: We prorate reserved GPU cost across active pipelines over the billing period; unused reserved capacity shows up as idle and you can set shared pool policies to reduce waste.
[04:53] Samir Khan: Any examples of realized savings?
[04:56] Lila Chen: We had a retail customer cut per-1M-token cost by ~36% by enabling KV caching and batching for top three routes plus switch to an 8-bit quantized variant. We can share an anonymized case study.
[05:07] Priya Patel: Please share that, that would help our finance team.
[05:10] Marco Alvarez: Will do. Also, the Optimize tab will give you concrete recommendations with estimated $ savings per month and confidence.
[05:18] Ethan Ross: For the POC, we want to measure throughput and cost under peak load. Can you run benchmarks in our Dedicated environment?
[05:25] Marco Alvarez: Yes, our bench harness can run synthetic traffic or replay sample traffic. For Dedicated Private we can run in a staging cluster with representative nodes.
[05:33] Maya Li: Who owns data from those tests? We need to ensure it doesn't leave our VPC.
[05:37] Marco Alvarez: For Private deployments it stays in your network; for hosted we scrub and keep only telemetry per the retention agreement. We'll put that in the security docs.
[05:45] [05:45] Lila Chen: Quick pause — any other questions so far?
[05:49] Priya Patel: Timeline — we want to go to POC within two weeks if pricing and security checks out.
[05:53] Lila Chen: Sounds doable. We'll follow up with pricing and SOC2 artifacts.
[05:57] Jordan Patel: Back to console — this is the alerts timeline for the "claims-processing" route, you can see a cost spike at 02/12 and the top contributing prompts.
[06:08] Samir Khan: That prompt list is helpful but can you anonymize?
[06:12] Marco Alvarez: Absolutely — masking is default for viewer roles.
[06:16] Ethan Ross: How do we instrument our app to surface trace ids back to Redwood for correlation?
[06:20] Jordan Patel: We support trace correlation headers; you can pass a request_id and it shows up in the per-call logs with latency, model, and tokens used.
[06:28] Priya Patel: Ok, last few items: can you produce an export of cost breakdown per route for last quarter?
[06:33] Marco Alvarez: Yes, exports to CSV or BigQuery, scheduled reports too.
[06:37] Maya Li: We'll need a redaction process for prompt text when exporting.
[06:40] Lila Chen: You can choose to strip prompts on export or replace with prompt hashes.
[06:45] [06:45] Ethan Ross: Great. Anything on SLA credits if Dedicated misses latency?
[06:49] Marco Alvarez: SLA details are in the contract; generally credits for sustained breaches beyond 3x window, and we include runbooks and on-call escalation for enterprise customers.
[06:59] Priya Patel: Perfect. On pricing, do you have a short deck with committed capacity tiers?
[07:03] Lila Chen: Yes we'll send that. Also note we have short-term reserved (monthly) and annual with discounts and burst capacity pricing.
[07:13] Samir Khan: For the POC, we prefer monthly reserved rather than hosted to mimic production.
[07:17] Marco Alvarez: That makes sense. We'll size and recommend a monthly reservation for the 2-week POC.
[07:24] Priya Patel: Ok let's move to the wrap and next steps.
[07:27] Lila Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing + contract template, Marco will share SOC2/ISO and architecture notes, customer will supply sample traffic and target spike patterns, and we'll tentatively schedule POC to start 2026-03-16.
[07:40] Ethan Ross: Sounds good. Any other blockers?
[07:43] Maya Li: Need to review security docs, but otherwise fine.
[07:46] Priya Patel: Finance will want the cost per 1M tokens example and the case study.
[07:50] Lila Chen: We'll include both in the follow-up.
[07:54] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links.
[07:57] Samir Khan: Thanks all.
[08:00] Meeting ended.
